key_insight: Charge-aware machine-learning potentials enable near-DFT-accuracy CrSBr simulations, revealing that sulfur vacancies can lower chromium Frenkel-pair migration barriers by up to 1.1 eV.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports defect engineering and analysis of electron-beam-driven structural changes in CrSBr for potential magneto-optoelectronic devices.
method: Develop and benchmark Cr–S–Br machine-learning interatomic potentials, including charge-aware qNEP.
Use nudged elastic band calculations to evaluate defect migration barriers.
Calculate atomic displacement thresholds to compare species susceptibility to electron-beam damage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-DFT accuracy for qNEP across lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and anisotropic pressure response, and identifies Br as the easiest species to displace.
watch_item: Accuracy for structures and conditions outside the benchmarked domain requires further validation before predictive use.
paper_title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
